explanations: There is none. Rows are pulled from a server-side cursor 500 at a time, and Readable.from over an async generator is pull-based, so stream.pipeline only asks for the next batch when res can accept more data; memory stays bounded by roughly one batch. If the client disconnects, pipeline rejects and destroys the source, and the finally block closes the cursor and releases the pooled connection on every path.

Readable.from(rows()) only advances the async generator when the readable needs data, and pipeline respects res's backpressure. So cursor.read is called at the client's pace. Nothing loads all rows up front, nothing reads on a timer, and Express does not spill responses to disk.

pipeline rejects on premature close of res and destroys the source; the catch logs it and the finally always closes the cursor and calls client.release(). Pool idle timeouts and crashes don't come into it.

Ties on departs_at would otherwise come back in arbitrary order, so repeated exports could differ. Cursors don't require a unique ordering, join strategy is unrelated, and the header is yielded by the generator before any rows.
